Score 0–100, chance = 0, 100 = perfect, higher is better ↑: a score, not a share of right answers. Not run: the model is not on that bench; Not applicable: the score does not apply (Combined without all three groups); the reason shows on hover or focus. Rank is the place by the score chosen among the models in view, 1, 2, 3 without repeats; models with the same score keep the table's order, which claims no difference (no bench's file carries an all-pairs test, so no tiers). A column head sorts by it; again, the other way.

How it's scored

  • Every bench on one scale: 0 = random guessing, 100 = perfect; higher is better ↑.
  • Turkish Reading (656 questions) and Turkish Grammar (1,542), 5 options each, English Reading (547 of the reading questions translated into English, 5 options) and Logic and Math: accuracy corrected for chance, (accuracy − 1/k) / (1 − 1/k) × 100, k the number of options. Vision: the same on Reading's 763 questions that depend on the printed page, read from the page image alone.
  • Backgammon: 0 = the error rate of a player that picks a random legal move, 100 = no error.
  • Combined = the plain mean of Reading · Turkish (all 2,198 Turkish questions), Logic & Math (pooled) and Backgammon, equal weights, as before the splits, only for a model that ran all three, one model on every bench (the rule).
  • Learning from experience ("did it improve?", points gained, higher is better ↑) is a column of its own, outside the combined score.
  • Lower is better ↓ for calibration error (ECE, in points: how far the stated probabilities are from the hit rate) and latency. Close scores read tied, never with an interval: the rule.

Methodology: every rule, the sources and how models are matched across benches.

Every request sent reasoning_effort "max"; 21.76 M of its 22.09 M output tokens were reasoning. The endpoint returned no token probabilities, so it answers with one letter, read from the reply; 46 of its 1,713 answers named no option and a random legal play was made. Each decision is billed at Meta's list price from the tokens OpenRouter reported.; hosted (API or subscription)

Backgammon76.93 of 25tied with KnowLine-31B-Gen1.5, REAX 1.3, Mammoth-1 and 1 more––backgammon:gemini-decision-1League 1; calibration definition pending Ümit; late entry: its own decisions in late-entry matches against League 1's field (different positions from the league's); scored against League 1's Random; provisional: played 17 of 19 matches; not played: GPT-6 Luna (Decisions API) (opponent's API out of credit); not played: Mercury Decide (opponent no longer served on OpenRouter); Google's Gemini Decision 1 through OpenRouter, pinned to Google AI Studio (fallbacks off) for every decision; never on our GPUs. Late entry to the original League 1 table (not in standings, not eligible for the Hype Cup); its matches were played on 11 Nov 2026. It played 17 of its 19 opponents: its pair with Mercury Decide was not played (Mercury Decide is no longer served on OpenRouter; match #1016 aborted) and its pair with GPT-6 Luna was not played (GPT-6 Luna's API was out of credit). Two runner builds: dab6da5 for its first 9 matches (#993–#1013, before 21:46:31 UTC), with no probability-map check, and 38024d6 (map-check v2) from 21:46:31 UTC for its last 8 (#1053–#1063). Under map-check v2 a returned probability map is used only if it covers exactly the options shown, every value is finite and in [0, 1], and the values sum to 1 within 1e-6; this sum rule is new (no frozen sum tolerance existed), was chosen on 11 Nov 2026 and applies to this entry only; a failed map still plays the returned choice and stores no probabilities. An offline audit of the first matches under the same rule found no failing map. Option order: we send the options in our seeded order, as for every setup, while Google's docs say the API sorts the option keys alphabetically (UTF-8 byte order; an exact tie goes to the alphabetically first key), so the order the model sees is probably not ours (Google's docs; not verified by us). Its cost is the billed cost of each decision; the entry, with its paid opponents, billed $1.1819 in all.; hosted (API or subscription)
